01.actor: a woman who came to Jerusalem with a child on her shoulders
01.event: She raised the child she carried, and when he grew up he had intercourse with her.
01.turn: They were brought to court on the presumption that he was her son, though that was not certain.
01.outcome: The court stoned both of them, not because he was definitely her son but because he clung to her.
01.summary: A woman came to Jerusalem with a child riding on her shoulders and raised him. When he grew up he had intercourse with her. They were brought to court and stoned, not because he was certainly her son but because he clung to her and so was presumed to be.

02.actor: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananya and a certain heretic
02.event: A heretic mocked Rabbi Yehoshua as a man of thorns, citing a verse.
02.turn: Rabbi Yehoshua called him a fool and sent him to read the rest of the verse, which turns the insult into praise.
02.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua explained the verse as meaning that Israel's best protect it, like thorns sealing a breach, or grind the nations down.
02.summary: A heretic told Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananya that a verse called Israel's best merely thorns. Rabbi Yehoshua called him a fool and pointed to the end of the verse. He then explained that the best of Israel protect the people like thorns in a breach, or crush the nations.

03.event: Rabbi Meir, who used to mock transgressors, saw Satan disguised as a woman across a river and crossed a rope bridge toward her.
03.turn: Halfway across, Satan dropped the disguise and said he would have destroyed Rabbi Meir but for the heavenly proclamation protecting him.
03.outcome: Rabbi Meir was spared only because of his standing in heaven, and was humbled.
03.summary: Rabbi Meir used to ridicule people who sinned. One day Satan appeared to him as a woman on the far side of a river. With no ferry, Rabbi Meir crossed on a rope bridge. Halfway over, Satan let him go and said that only the heavenly warning to be careful with Rabbi Meir and his Torah had saved him.

06.event: A reservoir at Yavne thought to be full was measured and found deficient, so Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva disagreed about the purifications already done in it.
06.turn: They argued with parables and analogies, and Rabbi Akiva's argument that disqualification here is of the thing itself, like a blemished priest, prevailed.
06.outcome: Rabbi Tarfon accepted Rabbi Akiva's reasoning and said that whoever separates from him separates from life.
06.summary: A reservoir at Yavne was thought to hold the required amount but, when measured, was found short. Rabbi Tarfon would declare earlier purifications in it pure and Rabbi Akiva impure, and they argued with parables. Rabbi Akiva's analysis won, and Rabbi Tarfon conceded.
06.missing: It is mostly a legal debate. The incident is only a framing, and nothing is said about the people who immersed.

07.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
07.event: Yeimar bar Hashu's agent seized a dead debtor's boat, and Rav Pappa and Rav Huna, who were also creditors, objected and then seized it themselves.
07.turn: Each claimed to own the whole boat, and a third sage challenged whether they could acquire it that way.
07.outcome: Rava rebuked them as white geese who strip people of their cloaks, since seizure after the debtor's death does not acquire anything.
07.summary: Yeimar bar Hashu sent his agent to seize a dead debtor's boat. Rav Pappa and Rav Huna told the agent that seizing it harmed other creditors, then seized the boat themselves and each claimed all of it. Rav Pineas objected and they came before Rava, who called them white geese who remove people's cloaks and said the seizure was invalid.

09.actor: a certain woman and the man guarding an executed body
09.event: A woman visiting her husband's grave had intercourse with a man guarding the body of someone executed by the king, and when that body was taken she proposed disinterring her husband as a substitute.
09.turn: The body the guard was watching disappeared.
09.outcome: She had her husband removed from his grave so the guard could claim he had done his job.
09.summary: A widow visiting her husband's grave had intercourse with a man guarding the body of an executed man. When that body was taken, she suggested digging up her husband so the guard could say he had done his duty, and she removed him from his grave. The Rabbis cite it to show sin is possible even in mourning.
09.missing: The Hebrew only alludes to the incident. The details come from the translator's gloss.

10.actor: Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter, as seen by Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok
10.event: Rabbi Elazar saw the daughter gathering barley kernels from between horses' hooves in Akko.
10.turn: She had once been very wealthy and was now reduced to scavenging.
10.outcome: He applied a verse to her, reading it as saying she must follow the flock to sustain her body.
10.summary: Rabbi Elazar swore he had seen Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter in Akko picking barley out of horse dung and hooves. He applied a verse about following the flock and read it as saying she must feed her own body from the leftovers.
10.missing: This is an eyewitness report. How she fell from wealth is only implied by the surrounding discussion.

12.event: Rav Kahana asked Rav Ashi to testify about something Rav Ashi did not at first remember.
12.turn: Rav Ashi eventually remembered and testified, and saw that Rav Kahana was hesitant, fearing he had put the testimony in his mind.
12.outcome: Rav Ashi told him he had not relied on him and had made the effort to remember the incident himself.
12.summary: Rav Ashi knew of testimony relevant to Rav Kahana. When Rav Kahana asked whether he remembered it, Rav Ashi said no, and then said he did not know. In the end he remembered and testified. Seeing Rav Kahana hesitant, he said he had not relied on him but had remembered it by his own effort.

14.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
14.event: They meant to permit a nursing mother to remarry at once, following a baraita, but an old woman said Rav Nahman had forbidden it to her.
14.turn: Rav Pappi showed them from a baraita and a ruling of Shmuel that the stricter view applied.
14.outcome: They admitted it had not been on their minds, and the ruling was set that remarriage is permitted if the child died and forbidden if she weaned him.
14.summary: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were about to act on a baraita letting a nursing mother remarry. An old woman said Rav Nahman had once forbidden it to her. Rav Pappi challenged them with another baraita and Shmuel's ruling, and they conceded they had forgotten it.
14.missing: It is mostly legal argument, with only a thin episode of the sages being corrected.

15.actor: Rav Nahman and a woman of Mehoza married in Neharde'a
15.event: The woman and her husband came before Rav Nahman about her marriage contract, and he noticed from her accent that she was from Mehoza.
15.turn: He first ruled by the custom of Babylonia, following Rav, then was told she had married into Neharde'a.
15.outcome: He reversed to rule by Shmuel's view, the custom of Neharde'a.
15.summary: A woman from Mehoza who had married a man in Neharde'a came before Rav Nahman about her marriage contract. He heard her accent and ruled by the Babylonian custom, following Rav. When told she had married into Neharde'a, he ruled by Neharde'a's custom, following Shmuel.

16.actor: Rav Pappa and Yehuda bar Mareimar
16.event: Rav Pappa went to write his son's marriage contract with the family of Abba of Sura, and Yehuda bar Mareimar came to greet him but would not go in.
16.turn: Rav Pappa overcame Yehuda's reluctance to enter, since his presence would pressure Abba into a large dowry.
16.outcome: Yehuda sat silent, Abba thought he was angry and wrote down all he owned as the dowry, then said he had left nothing for himself.
16.summary: Rav Pappa went to write the marriage contract for his son, and Yehuda bar Mareimar came to greet him. At the door Yehuda hesitated to enter, and Rav Pappa pressed him until he went in and sat silent. The bride's father took his silence for anger and wrote all his property into the dowry, and then said he had left nothing for himself.

20.actor: Reish Lakish, his disseminator Yehuda bar Nahmani, and the mourning Rav Hiyya bar Abba
20.event: After Rav Hiyya bar Abba's child died, Reish Lakish went on the second day with his disseminator to comfort him and had him speak in turn.
20.turn: The first words seemed to blame the dead child's generation, but are explained as saying Rav Hiyya was significant enough to be taken for the sins of the generation.
20.outcome: The disseminator spoke on God's praise, the mourners, the comforters and all Israel, which are the blessings recited in a house of mourning.
20.summary: Rav Hiyya bar Abba's child died. Reish Lakish did not visit on the first day. On the second he brought his disseminator and had him speak in turn on the dead child, God's praise, the mourners, those who comfort them and all Israel. The opening seemed to upset the mourner but meant he was important enough to be taken for the generation's sins.
20.missing: The sequence of speeches has no dramatic ending and serves mainly to give the text of the blessings.
